BipInput.description:

component names of the request.

component.description:

`component_names` (the resolved database name also works)

BlackOilCorrelationName.description:
Bubble-point, solution gas-oil ratio and oil formation volume factor
correlation. The three selectors share these names.

ComponentDef.description:
EOS component definition for a component that is not in the built-in
database.

carbon_number_range.description: Width of a pseudo-component's carbon-number range (optional)

is_pure.description: True for a pure component, false for a pseudo-component (default true)

molecular_weight.description: Molecular weight in g/mol (`molar_mass` is accepted as an alias)

name.description:
Component name; binary interaction entries refer to it. A database
name or short code (for example "methane" or "C1") also supplies the
component's ideal-gas heat capacity for thermal properties.

parachor.description:
Parachor for interfacial tension (optional; estimated from the
molecular weight by Quayle's correlation when omitted)

specific_gravity.description:
Liquid specific gravity at standard conditions (optional). With the
boiling point (or the molecular weight) it also supplies a Kesler-Lee
ideal-gas heat capacity for thermal properties.

volume_shift.description:
Peneloux volume shift parameter s (optional; `volume_shift_s` is
accepted as an alias)

oneOf.description: de Waard-Lotz with the Mariaca H2S regime factor.

Peng-Robinson, with the 1978 alpha function for acentric factors above
0.49. Default.

EosViscosityModelName.description: Phase viscosity model for the EOS property report.

oneOf.description: Chosen from the phase's reduced density and molecular weight. Default.
Wilke mixing rule over pure-component low-pressure gas viscosities.
Pedersen corresponding states with a methane reference.
Yarranton expanded-fluid model (heavy oils, all densities).

FailureKind.description: Why the call failed. `invalid_input` is the caller's to fix and is not charged; `computation_failed` means the calculation ran and produced no answer, which consumed compute and IS charged; `internal` is ours and is not charged.

FlashEosModelName.description:
Equation of state for `run_eos_flash`: the two cubics, or GERG-2008 for
single-phase gas properties.

oneOf.description:
Peng-Robinson, with the 1978 alpha function for acentric factors above
0.49. Default.

GERG-2008 reference equation for natural gases (Kunz and Wagner, 2012).
Single phase only: the fluid is treated as one gas phase whatever its
state, with no phase split. Covers 21 components: methane to n-decane,
nitrogen, carbon dioxide, hydrogen sulfide, water, oxygen, argon,
helium, hydrogen and carbon monoxide.

FlashTypeName.description: Which pair of state variables the flash is specified by.

oneOf.description:
Pressure and molar enthalpy: solves for the temperature at which the
feed's molar enthalpy equals `enthalpy_j_per_mol`.

Pressure and molar entropy: solves for the temperature at which the
feed's molar entropy equals `entropy_j_per_mol_k`.

angle.description:
Inclination [degrees from vertical], as elsewhere on the platform.
Accepted but not used, for the same reason as roughness.

heat_transfer_coefficient.description:
Overall heat-transfer coefficient [W/m2/K] (default 0), for the
temperature profile

roughness.description:
Absolute roughness [m] (default 4.5e-5). Accepted so a pipe geometry
can be passed unchanged; the profile does not use it, because the
converged inlet and outlet pressures already carry the friction loss.

surrounding_temperature.description: Surrounding temperature [K] (default 277), for the temperature profile

FlowCorrelationName.description: Canonical name of a multiphase pressure-drop correlation.

FluidConfig.description:
Black-oil fluid definition: the reference (standard-condition) properties
and the correlation used for each property. Every correlation has a
default, so only `fluid_type` is required.

formation_volume_factor_correlation.description:
Oil formation volume factor (Bo) correlation (default: the
saturation_pressure_correlation)

reference_gas_mw.description:
Gas molecular weight in g/mol; the gas gravity is this over 28.97
(default: 20.279)

salinity.description: Water salinity in ppm (water fluid type only; default 0)

solution_gas_ratio_correlation.description:
Solution gas-oil ratio (Rs) correlation (default: the
saturation_pressure_correlation)

FluidConfigInputParams.description:
Fluid flow rates and PVT configuration used by equipment and thermal tools.
Rates are at standard conditions. `gas_rate` is the total produced gas: with
oil present the oil holds `oil_rate × dissolved_gas_ratio` of it in solution,
liberated below its bubble point, and only the excess is free gas; with no
oil all of it is free gas.

dissolved_gas_ratio.description:
Dissolved gas-oil ratio in Sm3/Sm3. Default: gas_rate / oil_rate when
both are given, otherwise 90. Set 0 for a dead oil.

gas_rate.description: Total gas rate in Sm3/day (free plus solution gas).

FluidTypeName.description: Fluid phase type for property calculations.

GasCriticalPropertiesCorrelationName.description: Gas pseudo-critical properties correlation (from gas gravity).

oneOf.description:
Lee, Gonzalez and Eakin refitted by Viswanathan (2007) to pure methane
at 34 to 207 MPa and 310 to 478 K. For methane and methane-rich gases
only: its K reaches zero at a gas molecular weight of 17.49 g/mol, and
from there the `lee` value is returned.

Carr, Kobayashi and Burrows (1954) viscosity at atmospheric pressure,
in Standing's fit. Has no pressure dependence.
Dranchuk and Abou-Kassem with modified coefficients.

Gopal (1977) piecewise fits to the Standing-Katz chart, for
pseudo-reduced pressures 0.2 to 15 and temperatures 1.05 to 3.0.

HeaterCoolerModeName.description:
Heater/cooler operating mode, spelt as the network `heater_cooler_data.mode`.
Every mode closes the energy balance Q = ṁ·cp·(T_out − T_in) on the stream's
mass rate and mass-weighted heat capacity at the inlet state.

oneOf.description: `heat_duty` is given and the outlet temperature follows.
`outlet_temperature` is given and the duty follows.

The outlet sits `approach_temperature` short of `utility_temperature`:
above it for a cooler, below it for a heater, and never past the inlet
temperature.

ε-NTU against an isothermal utility at `utility_temperature` with
conductance `ua`: T_out = T_in + (T_util − T_in)·(1 − exp(−UA/(ṁ·cp))).

HydrateModelName.description:
Hydrate thermodynamics. `vdwp_combined` runs both structures and reports the
warmer, controlling envelope; the single-structure variants force one.

oneOf.description: Tier-1 screening correlation from gas specific gravity.
van der Waals-Platteeuw + Parrish-Prausnitz, structure I.
Structure II — lifted by even ~1% propane.
Both structures, warmer envelope wins. Default.
Mechanical skin of a `darcy` or `fetkovich` model.
A and B of the `forchheimer_ab` gas deliverability equation.
A and B of the `fetkovich_ab` oil deliverability equation.
Fortsch and Whitman, evaluated at standard conditions.

OilViscosityCorrelationName.description: Oil viscosity correlation (dead, saturated and undersaturated oil).

PipeEnd.description:
End of a pipe: `top` is the end the pipe angle points towards, `bottom`
the end it is measured from.

phase_rates_ksm3_day.description:
Volumetric phase rates at standard conditions [kSm³/day —
thousand standard cubic metres per day], in the canonical
[gas, oil, water] order. Same unit as the solver's MassFlow
dataclass (`gas_phase_rate` / `oil_phase_rate` / `water_phase_rate`).

oneOf.description:
Kesler and Lee (1976) critical temperature and pressure from the
specific gravity and boiling point. Default.

Twu (1984) perturbation from the n-alkane reference, from the specific
gravity and boiling point.

Sancet critical temperature and pressure from the molecular weight
alone.

PumpCentrifugalParams.description:
Multistage centrifugal pump: sections of identical stages on one shaft,
each on a water stage curve at its reference speed, run at `speed` by the
affinity laws H = s²·h(Q/s), η = η(Q/s) with s = speed / reference_speed.

efficiency_factor.description: Multiplier on stage efficiency, for wear or calibration (default 1).

head_factor.description: Multiplier on stage head, for wear or calibration (default 1).

sections.description: Sections in flow order, suction first.

stages_per_step.description:
Largest number of stages evaluated at one fluid state. The stream is
re-evaluated at the inlet of every step, so free gas compresses and
redissolves along the pump. Default: one step per section.

viscosity_correction.description: Viscosity correction of the water stage curves (default none).

PumpEspCableParams.description: ESP power cable from surface to motor.

temperature.description: Conductor temperature in K. Default: the pump suction temperature.

PumpEspMotorParams.description: ESP motor nameplate at the base frequency.

load_curve.description:
Efficiency and power factor against load. Default: a generic ESP
induction-motor curve.

outer_diameter.description:
Motor housing outer diameter in m. With `casing_inner_diameter` it gives
the fluid velocity past the motor.

rated_voltage.description: Rated voltage, line to line, in V.

PumpEspParams.description:
Electrical submersible pump drive train: motor, cable and surface
equipment. The drive frequency is `base_frequency` × `speed` / the first
section's `reference_speed`; motor power and voltage scale with it.

base_frequency.description:
Frequency the first section's stage curve and the motor nameplate are
rated at, in Hz (default 60).

cable.description: Power cable. Omitted: no cable losses.

casing_inner_diameter.description:
Casing inner diameter at the motor in m, for the fluid velocity past
the motor.

max_intake_gas_fraction.description:
Free-gas volume fraction at the intake (0-1) above which gas
interference is reported.

seal_power.description: Seal and protector shaft power in W (default 0).

PumpMotorLoadCurveParams.description: Motor efficiency and power factor against load, load strictly increasing.

load.description: Shaft power over available motor power (dimensionless).

PumpSectionParams.description: A run of identical stages on the pump shaft.

bep_flow.description:
Best-efficiency flow per stage in m3/s at `reference_speed`. Default:
the efficiency peak of the stage curve.

max_flow.description:
Upper end of the recommended operating range: flow per stage in m3/s
at `reference_speed`.

min_flow.description:
Lower end of the recommended operating range: flow per stage in m3/s
at `reference_speed`.

reference_speed.description: Speed the stage curve was measured at, in rpm.

stages.description: Number of stages in the section.

PumpStageCurveParams.description: Water performance of one pump stage at its section's `reference_speed`.

efficiency.description:
Hydraulic efficiency per stage (0-1), one value per flow point. Optional:
a section without it runs at the pump's `efficiency`.

flow.description: Flow per stage in m3/s (in situ), strictly increasing, at least two points.

head.description: Head per stage in m, one value per flow point.

PumpViscosityCorrectionName.description: Correction of the water stage curves for liquid viscosity.

oneOf.description: Water curves used as tested. Default.

ANSI/HI 9.6.7. Needs a best-efficiency point on every section: an
efficiency curve or `bep_flow`.

Wilson-seeded successive substitution with a Newton update on the
unknown pressure or temperature. Fast; can fail near the critical
point and in retrograde regions. A composition with a component whose
acentric factor exceeds 0.9 is moved to `envelope` automatically.
Default.

Simultaneous Newton with an analytic Jacobian, well conditioned as the
K-values approach one. Falls back to `classical` if it fails.

Runs the classical method from several seeds (Wilson, inverse Wilson,
a pressure scan) and keeps the best. About five times the classical
cost.

Bubble point: the feed is liquid and an incipient vapour appears.
Default.
Dew point: the feed is vapour and an incipient liquid appears.

SlipModelName.description:
Slip model for the Sachdeva choke model: how the gas-liquid velocity ratio
at the choke inlet is estimated.

StageSpecParams.description: One stage of a multi-stage centrifugal compressor.

ToolResponse.description: The standard response envelope. `result` is the tool's own payload; its shape is documented per tool in the operator guide.

WaterAnalysisParams.description:

`flow_assurance.water_analysis` in a network. Shared by the scale and
acid-gas-partitioning tools.

bicarbonate_mg_per_l.description:

closure diagnostic, not as a constraint on the in-situ speciation.

iron_mg_per_l.description: Total dissolved iron as Fe2+ [mg/l] - siderite

WaxActivityModelName.description: Activity model for the Tier-3 wax SLE flash.

oneOf.description: Regular-solution theory with Won solubility parameters. Default.

Unit activity coefficients, which reduces the flash to the Won
ideal solid solution.
Tier-1 correlation from a C7+ characterisation. Default.

bearerAuth.description: A short-lived access token. Exchange your API key for one at the platform's `POST /oauth/token` (the user API, not this host): send the key as `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>` with `grant_type=client_credentials`, form or JSON encoded, then send the returned token here as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. The official clients do this for you and refresh the token before it expires.

info.description:
Physics-based production-network solving, PVT/EOS, flow assurance and transient multiphase flow.

**Units are SI throughout** — pressure MPa, temperature K, rates kSm³/day, lengths m. Permeability in millidarcy is the single exception.

Every operation costs credits, quoted per tool in `x-graphsolve-credits` as `base_credits + ceil(max(0, wall_ms - free_ms) / ms_per_credit)`. Catalogue lookups are free.

schema.description: Input for decline-curve generation (raw JSON string).

decline_json.description:
Decline-generation request: `{kind, params, times | t_max, n_points
(default 200), economic_limit?}`. `params` is keyed by name for each
`kind` (q rate, t time):
- `arps`: `initial_rate`, `initial_decline_rate`,
  `hyperbolic_exponent`; q = qi/(1 + b·Di·t)^(1/b), exponential at
  b = 0 and harmonic at b = 1 (Arps, 1945).
- `modified_hyperbolic`: the `arps` names plus
  `minimum_decline_rate`; hyperbolic until the instantaneous decline
  falls to it, exponential after.
- `duong`: `intercept` (q1), `slope` (a), `time_exponent` (m);
  q = q1·t^(−m)·exp(a/(1 − m)·(t^(1−m) − 1)) (Duong, 2011).
- `stretched_exponential`: `initial_rate`, `characteristic_time` (τ),
  `exponent` (n); q = qi·exp(−(t/τ)^n) (Valkó, 2009).
- `power_law_exponential`: `initial_rate`, `initial_loss_ratio` (Di),
  `infinite_loss_ratio` (D∞), `exponent` (n); q = qi·exp(−D∞·t −
  (Di − D∞)/n·t^n) (after Ilk et al., 2008).

Rates and times are in any consistent units, and decline rates are
per unit of that time. Returns time, rate and cumulative arrays.

inflow_model.description:
The inflow model: the same object as a row of a network's `sources`
library. Always `inflow_model_id` (any string) and `ipr_model`. Every
model except `table` also needs `reservoir_pressure` [MPa],
`reservoir_temperature` [K] and a black-oil `fluid` (`fluid_type`,
`reference_oil_density` [kg/m³], `reference_gas_mw` [g/mol],
`dissolved_gas_ratio` [Sm³/Sm³], `saturation_pressure_correlation`,
`oil_viscosity_correlation`, optional `salinity` [ppm]). `watercut` is
water/(water+oil) in percent (0-100) on the oil models; on
`forchheimer`, `forchheimer_ab`, `vertical_gas_pss`,
`fractured_vertical_gas_pss` and a transient model with a gas fluid it
is the water-gas ratio [Sm³/Sm³]. Those four gas deliverability models
read `fluid.dissolved_gas_ratio` as the condensate-gas ratio
[Sm³/Sm³]; a transient model with a gas fluid produces no condensate.

Fields each `ipr_model` needs (permeability mD, lengths m, areas m²):
- `table`: `ipr_table`, a list of points `{oil_rate, gas_rate,
  water_rate [kSm³/day], pressure [MPa], temperature [K]}`; no fluid.
- `pi`: `reservoir_properties.productivity_index` [Sm³/day/MPa of
  liquid at standard conditions], `watercut`.
- `darcy`: `reservoir_properties.permeability`,
  `well_properties.{wellbore_radius, skin}`,
  `reservoir_dimensions.{drainage_area, reservoir_thickness_tst,
  dietz_shape_factor}`, `watercut`.
- `fetkovich`: the `darcy` fields plus `relative_permeability`, one
  Corey entry `{phase, residual_saturation, permeability_endpoint,
  exponent}` for each of oil, water and gas.

  [Sm³/day/MPa²]}` in q = a·(pr − psat) + b·(psat² − pwf²), with the
  bubble point psat from `fluid`.
- `forchheimer`: `reservoir_properties.permeability`,
  `well_properties.{wellbore_radius, skin, perforation_interval}`,
  `reservoir_dimensions.{drainage_area, reservoir_thickness_tst}`,
  `relative_permeability` (as for `fetkovich`), `watercut`.
- `forchheimer_ab`: `ipr_coefficients.{a [MPa²·day/Sm³], b
  [MPa²·day²/Sm⁶]}` in pr² − pwf² = a·q + b·q².
- `vertical_gas_pss`: `reservoir_properties.permeability`,
  `well_properties.{wellbore_radius, skin}`,
  `reservoir_dimensions.{drainage_area, reservoir_thickness_tst}`;
  optional `well_properties.perforation_interval`.
- `fractured_vertical_gas_pss`: the `vertical_gas_pss` fields (skin
  optional) plus `fracture_properties.half_length` and either
  `fracture_properties.fcd` or `fracture_properties.conductivity`

  perforation_interval}` (the perforated height).
- `faulted`: `well_properties.wellbore_radius`,
  `reservoir_dimensions.fault_distance`; `fault_config` `single`
  (default), `corner`, `intersecting` (with `fault_angle_deg`) or
  `channel` (with `channel_width`).

  `reservoir_properties.{stimulated_permeability, stimulated_radius}`;
  optional `stimulated_porosity`, `stimulated_compressibility`.
- `horizontal`: `well_properties.{wellbore_radius,
  perforation_interval}` (the completed lateral length).

  `reservoir_dimensions.{reservoir_length_x, reservoir_length_y}`;
  optional `fracture_properties.conductivity_type`.
- `horizontal_msf`: `fracture_properties.{half_length, width,
  permeability}` and optional `number_of_fractures` (default 1),

The optimisation counterpart of solve_network.

schema.description: Input for a network optimisation (raw JSON string).

optimisation_json.description:
Optimisation request: `network_payload` (a model-format network, as
for `solve_network`), `variables`, `objective`, `constraints` and
optional `settings`. Elements are referenced by id: `{"node_id":
"<id>"}` or `{"edge_id": "<id>"}`.

- `variables`: `{id, variable_type, element, lower_bound,
  upper_bound, initial_value?}` each. The control types and their
  units: `choke_opening` (choke bean diameter, m; edge),
  `gas_lift_rate` (kSm³/day; node only, the gas-injection source),
  `pipe_diameter` and `pipe_roughness` (m; edge, optional
  `segment_index` in the element), `source_rate` (total kSm³/day at
  fixed composition; node), `source_water_cut` (percent 0-100, the
  water-gas ratio on a gas fluid; node), `source_gor` (Sm³/Sm³, the
  condensate-gas ratio on a gas fluid; node), `boundary_pressure`
  (MPa; source or sink node, the reservoir pressure of an IPR
  source), `compressor_ratio` (edge, fixed-ratio machines),
  `compressor_speed` (rad/s; edge), `separator_pressure` (MPa; node),
  `source_temperature` (K; node), `heater_duty` (W; edge),
  `pump_speed` (rpm; edge) and `pump_frequency` (Hz; edge, an ESP
  drive).
- `objective`: `{terms: [...]}`, each term tagged by `type`:
  `maximise_phase_rate` and `minimise_phase_rate` `{phase, elements,
  weight (default 1)}`; `maximise_revenue` `{terms: [{phase, price
  (per kSm³), elements}]}`; `minimise_pressure_drop` and
  `minimise_power_consumption` `{elements, weight}`;
  `minimise_deviation` `{observations: [{element, quantity,
  measured_value, weight}]}`. A `phase` is `oil`, `water`, `gas`,
  `free_gas`, `liquid` or `total_mass` (the total volumetric rate); a
  `quantity` is `{"phase_rate": "<phase>"}` or one of `pressure`,
  `temperature`, `pressure_drop`, `velocity`, `power`,
  `pump_npsh_margin`, `pump_flow_range_margin`, `pump_motor_load`,
  `pump_intake_gas_fraction`.
- `constraints`: `{id, type, ...}` each, `type` one of
  `phase_rate_upper_bound` and `phase_rate_lower_bound` `{phase,
  elements, limit [kSm³/day]}`; `pressure_upper_bound` and
  `pressure_lower_bound` [MPa], `temperature_upper_bound` and
  `temperature_lower_bound` [K], `velocity_upper_bound` [m/s],
  `power_upper_bound` [W], each `{elements, limit}` on the sum over
  the elements; `pump_npsh_margin_lower_bound` [m],
  `pump_flow_range_lower_bound`, `pump_motor_load_upper_bound` and
  `pump_intake_gas_fraction_upper_bound` (fractions), each `{elements,
  limit}` held at every listed pump; `total_resource_limit`
  `{variable_ids, limit}` on the sum of those variables, in their
  unit.
- `settings`: `max_iter` (default 200), `tol` (1e-4), `max_cpu_time`
  (60 s), `print_level` (5), `gradient_method` (`sensitivity`, the
  default, or `finite_difference`) and `degeneracy_check` (default
  true: probe the free directions at the answer and report flat ones
  in `diagnostics`). `acceptable_tol` is accepted but not yet used.

The result carries `status`, `objective_value`, each variable's
initial and optimised value, each constraint's value and whether it
holds, `iterations`, and the solved network in `network_output`.

schema.description: Input for a time-series production forecast (raw JSON string).

forecast_json.description:
Forecast request: `network_payload` (a model-format network, as for
`solve_network`) and `time` are required. Elements are referenced by
id: `{"node_id": "<id>"}` or `{"edge_id": "<id>"}`.

- `time`: `start` (ISO-8601 date or date-time), `unit` (`minutes`,
  `hours`, `days` (default), `weeks`, `months`, `years`),
  `timestep_duration` (default 1) and either `num_timesteps` or
  `end_date`. Months and years are calendar lengths and need a
  whole-number `timestep_duration`.
- `engine`: omit for a plain solve each step, or `{type: solve,
  solver_settings: {max_iter (default 10), tolerance (default
  1e-6)}}`, or `{type: optimise, variables, objective, constraints,
  settings, iteration_report (default 1)}` with the
  `optimise_network` shapes. Each step's solve currently takes its
  iteration limit and tolerance from the network's `solve_parameters`
  (defaults 100 and 1e-6), which override `solver_settings`.
- `updates`: time-series drivers `{id, target, trigger, driver,
  condition?}`. `target` is `{target: network, elements: <selector>,
  property: <control type as for optimise_network>}`; the forms
  `{target: optimiser_control_bound, variable_id, bound: lower |
  upper | initial}`, `{target: optimiser_constraint_limit,
  constraint_id}` and `{target: optimiser_objective_term, term_index,
  field: {field: weight} | {field: price, phase}}` are accepted but
  not yet applied. `trigger` is `{on: time}` (x = elapsed time in
  `time.unit` at the start of the step), `{on: cumulative_production,
  key}` or `{on: property, source: <element>, property}`. `driver` is
  `{kind: constant, value}`, `{kind: linear, intercept,
  slope_per_unit_time, floor?, cap?}`, `{kind: decline, decline:
  exponential | hyperbolic | harmonic, qi, d, b (default 0.5)}` (d per
  unit of x) or `{kind: table, xs, ys, interp: linear | step}`.
  `condition` is `{compare: greater_than | less_than | greater_equal |
  less_equal, threshold}`, tested on x.
- `events`: `{timestep | at (ISO-8601), action}` each, `action` one
  of `{action: shutdown, element: <selector>}`, `{action: startup,
  element: <selector>}`, `{action: set_property, target, value}` (a
  lasting override, `target` as in updates) and `{action: workover,
  element: <selector>, downtime_steps, improvement_factor}` (shut in
  for `downtime_steps`; the improvement factor is not yet applied).
- A `<selector>` is `{select: element, element: <element>}`,
  `{select: group, group: <name>}` (a key of `groups`, which maps
  names to element lists) or `{select: all_pressure_sources}`.
- `transient_wells`: `{node_id, rate_history: [{time_hours, rate}]}`
  for each well whose IPR is a transient model.
- `failure_policy`: `{policy: continue_with_last}` (default: a step
  that fails carries the last good rates), `{policy: abort}`, or
  `{policy: retry_substep, splits}` (the retry is not yet
  implemented; the failed step's own rates are kept).
- `result_detail`: `summary` (default), `elements` (adds each
  element's results per step) or `full_snapshots` (adds the solved
  network per step; very large).
- `stream_results` (default true) only matters to callers that
  receive per-step progress; this tool returns the whole run at once.

Rates and cumulatives are keyed `node_<element id>_<phase>` (phase
oil, gas, water or total) in kSm³/day and kSm³. A
`cumulative_production` trigger key currently names the node by its
0-based position among the network's node elements (`node_0_oil`),
not by element id.

schema.description: Input for a transient pipe-flow run (raw JSON string).

transient_json.description:
Transient request, as a JSON object or a JSON string. Pressure MPa,
rates kSm3/day at standard conditions, temperature K, lengths m.

Pipe and fluid, in one of two forms:
- Network: `network_payload` (a model-format network: `format`,
  `elements`, `fluids`, `sources`) and `path`: `{"select": "edges",
  "edges": [{"edge_id": "<id>"}, ...]}`, the pipe edges of one route
  listed INLET FIRST. They are joined in that order and not checked for
  continuity; each keeps its drawn direction (`source` upstream) and lays
  out its `pipe_geometry` segments from `source` to `target` in the
  order given (survey stations by measured depth). Only the geometry
  and the fluid are read from the network:
  the fluid named by the first edge's source node, or the only fluid.
  Annulus and zero-length restriction segments are not represented.
- Bare: `segments` listed OUTLET FIRST, and `fluid`, a network fluid
  entry `{id, model_type, model}`. A segment has `pipe_length` m,
  `pipe_diameter` m and `pipe_angle` in degrees from vertical along the
  flow (0 flowing up, 90 horizontal, 180 flowing down), and optionally
  `pipe_roughness` m (default 4.6e-5), `max_cell_length` m (this
  segment only), and `surrounding_temperature` K with
  `heat_transfer_coefficient` W/(m2 K) (both, for heat exchange).

Black-oil and table fluids are read from `reference_oil_density`,
`dissolved_gas_ratio`, `reference_gas_mw` and `salinity` only, through
a fixed black-oil correlation set; `fluid_type`, correlation choices
and `pvt_table` are ignored. An equation-of-state fluid is tabulated
over (P, T) first.

`time`: `total` in `unit` (`seconds`, `minutes`, `hours` or `days`;
default `hours`), and `record_interval_s`, the recording interval in
seconds whatever the unit (default 30).

`boundary`, the state at t = 0: `outlet_pressure` MPa (for a choke, the
pressure downstream of it); inlet `oil_rate`, `water_rate` and
`gas_rate` kSm3/day, where `gas_rate` is the total gas, dissolved
included, and an omitted rate is 0; `inlet_temperature` K;
`water_salinity` ppm of the water entering; and `outlet`:
`{"type": "pressure"}` (default), `{"type": "closed"}` or
`{"type": "choke", "area": <m2>, "cd": <default 0.84>}`.
`outlet_pressure`, `inlet_temperature` and a non-zero rate are
required in both forms; nothing is taken from the network's nodes. The
run starts from the steady state of this boundary, and Graphsolve-Flux
needs a `pressure` outlet at t = 0.

`schedule`: `[{"at": <time in time.unit>, "set": {<boundary fields>}}]`.
Fields not set carry forward. Rates, `outlet_pressure`, choke `area` and
`water_salinity` ramp linearly from the previous event (t = 0 counts as
one), so a lone event at 0.5 h is a 30-minute ramp starting at t = 0;
a `water_salinity` not given at t = 0 applies from the previous event
instead. `inlet_temperature`, choke `cd` and the outlet `type` step at
the event. For a step in a ramped value, add an event with an empty `set`
at the same `at`, listed first. The outlet and the inlet rates are the
only valve controls: close the outlet for a valve slam, set the rates
to 0 for a shut-in.

`results`: `detail` is `summary` (default: pressure, gas_fraction and
mixture_velocity at the outlet and inlet cells), `profiles` (the
`variables` listed, default those three, at every `cell_stride`-th
cell plus both ends, or at the `cells` listed by index from 0 at the
outlet) or `full` (every variable the scheme carries, every cell;
`variables`, `cell_stride` and `cells` are ignored). Variables:
pressure, temperature, gas_fraction, liquid_holdup, gas_velocity,
liquid_velocity, mixture_velocity, mixture_density, oil_fraction,
salinity, solution_gor, sound_speed. Responses over about two million
values are refused.

`discretisation`: `max_cell_length` m (default 50).

`pvt`, for an equation-of-state fluid only: the table's `p_min_mpa`,
`p_max_mpa`, `t_min_k` and `t_max_k` (inferred from the geometry and
boundary when omitted; outside them properties are held at the edge)
and `pressure_nodes` (default 240) and `temperature_nodes` (default
24). The table's water is fresh water; `salinity_ppm` does not change
it.

Each scheme holds its cells in a pressure window and clamps anything
outside it: Flux 0.5-15 MPa (and 250-450 K), Wave 0.01-50 MPa, Field
0.05-100 MPa. Solver options cannot be set. `solver` is set from the
tool.

The result is `stats` (cells, length_m, simulated_s, steps, ...) and
`recording`: `geometry` of the recorded cells, `time_s`, `n_cells`,
and `series` of `{variable, unit, values}` with
`values[sample * n_cells + cell]`.
